edges.mechanism: The calcium in Ca-AKG (about 22% by mass) may bind levothyroxine in the gut and reduce absorption. The label advises separating calcium carbonate and other phosphate binders from levothyroxine by at least 4 hours.
edges.evidence: FDA label statement for calcium-containing binders; inferred from calcium content, no Ca-AKG-specific study.

edges.mechanism: Calcium (a multivalent cation) chelates fluoroquinolones and lowers their absorption. Take ciprofloxacin at least 2 h before or 6 h after calcium-containing products.
edges.evidence: FDA ciprofloxacin label; class effect inferred for Ca-AKG from calcium content.

edges.mechanism: Calcium chelates tetracyclines and impairs their absorption.
edges.evidence: FDA doxycycline/tetracycline label; inferred from calcium content.

edges.mechanism: Calcium supplements interfere with absorption of oral bisphosphonates such as alendronate, so doses should be separated.
edges.evidence: FDA alendronate label; inferred from calcium content.

edges.mechanism: Thiazides reduce urinary calcium excretion and may raise serum calcium. Supplemental calcium adds to the risk of hypercalcemia and calcium-alkali syndrome.
edges.evidence: FDA hydrochlorothiazide label plus review of calcium-alkali syndrome; no Ca-AKG-specific data.

edges.mechanism: Vitamin D increases calcium absorption. Long-term vitamin D raised hypercalcemia (RR 1.54) and hypercalciuria (RR 1.64), and calcium plus D3 raised kidney stones in WHI. Ca-AKG adds to the calcium load.
edges.evidence: Meta-analysis of RCTs plus a large RCT (WHI) for calcium/vitamin D; no Ca-AKG-specific data.

edges.mechanism: Doses add up. Ca-AKG supplies about 0.22 g elemental calcium per gram, and 1 g/day supplemental calcium increased kidney stones in WHI. A contested meta-analysis linked calcium supplements to myocardial infarction (HR 1.31).
edges.evidence: Large RCT and patient-level meta-analysis for calcium supplements; calcium share calculated from the formula.

edges.mechanism: Overlapping AKG content when combined with other AKG salts (OKG, AAKG). No interaction studies; total AKG dose rises.
edges.evidence: Small RCTs of other AKG salts at 10-20 g/day reported good tolerance; combinations not studied.

edges.mechanism: Added calcium load can worsen hypercalcemia. Calcium-alkali syndrome (hypercalcemia, metabolic alkalosis, renal impairment) follows high calcium intake.
edges.evidence: Review of calcium-alkali syndrome; drug label noting hypercalcemia may signal hidden hyperparathyroidism. Inferred for Ca-AKG.

edges.mechanism: Supplemental calcium, especially with vitamin D, increased incident kidney stones.
edges.evidence: Large RCT (WHI, n=36,282); inferred for Ca-AKG from calcium content.

edges.mechanism: In CKD, calcium-salt supplements raise serum calcium and change calcium-phosphate balance. In dialysis, AKG has been given with calcium carbonate as a phosphate-binding regimen. Use belongs within renal care.
edges.evidence: Meta-analysis of calcium keto-acid salts (not Ca-AKG) showing higher serum calcium; uncontrolled dialysis study of AKG.

edges.mechanism: In hyperlipidemic mice, AKG worsened plaque inflammation through OXGR1, while another mouse model showed protection after MI. Calcium supplements without vitamin D were linked to MI in a contested meta-analysis.
edges.evidence: Conflicting animal data; human signal only for calcium supplements. Very low certainty.

edges.mechanism: Calcium salts can raise measured serum calcium; ketoanalogue calcium salts raised serum calcium in CKD trials. This is a true physiological change, not an assay artifact.
edges.evidence: Meta-analysis of a related calcium-salt product; no Ca-AKG lab data.
